component.name: postmortem
component.summary: Review your Lichess and chess.com games

description.p: postmortem reviews your chess games locally with Stockfish: every move gets a classification from brilliant to blunder, and a coach explains in plain words why a move was bad – a hanging piece, an allowed fork, a missed mate.

ul.li: Loads your games from Lichess and chess.com, works offline afterwards
Move classifications, accuracy, eval graph and a live engine
Explore variations and replay your own mistakes as exercises
Statistics of your weaknesses across all your games
Puzzle training from the Lichess puzzle database, picked for your weaknesses

description.p: Your own opening repertoire as a tree: one move per position, the opponent's replies with how often they come up at your level, coverage, gaps you can fill by playing on the board, and your theory mistakes marked at the move. Flashcards now ask one move at a time; courses add what you learn to your repertoire. Learned lines are carried over (with a backup of the database first).

The Learn tab brings everything together: four tiles (flashcards, mistakes from your games, learning, exploring), one list of the openings you learn and play with recommendations from your games, and the positions where you leave theory. From a mistake you can now learn the whole opening line that leads to it.

Opening courses focus on what is played at your level: lines that come up in at least 3 in 100 games in your Lichess rating group (via the Lichess opening explorer) and lines from your own games; rare sidelines are listed apart. A new line enters the flashcards only after one run without arrows and without mistakes.

German opening names when the interface is set to German (game list, review, coach, Learn, Explore, statistics), and a game list that fits small windows: the source switch and the sync buttons wrap instead of being squeezed.

Your own flashcards from reviews, explored positions and bot games, with Stockfish's best moves; the openings tab becomes "Learn" with Flashcards and Explore; three weaker bots from ~400 Elo; resetting an opening's progress; clicking the active tab returns to its start.

Search and filter the game list (opponent, opening, result, colour, time control, own mistakes), favourite games, your accuracy as a coloured bar in the list, backup and restore of all your data, and a board that stays square after leaving fullscreen.
Free play gets start, back, forward and end under the board; the board buttons and player rows no longer shift while reviewing a game.

Free play for openings: play an opening freely and see which moves can come – from your own games, the opening theory and, with a personal Lichess token, how often each move is played on Lichess at your level. Optionally the opponent moves by frequency and Stockfish rates the candidates.

New start page for openings (learn, review, mistakes from your games), guided lessons that go through a line move by move with explanations, main lines before sidelines, and built-in sounds as loud as your recordings.

Opening training: explanations for every move from the Wikibooks opening theory, progress shown like a flashcard box, a back button and "learn again with arrows". Move sounds now play reliably through the sound card, and the Flatpak can play sound at all.
Fair play: games that are still running are not analysed (Lichess links, PGN imports), so you can't break the sites' rules by accident.
See whether your mistakes are getting fewer over time; new games are analysed automatically in the background after syncing.
The coach describes your opponent's moves from their side instead of addressing you, praises completed development and castling, and the move list scrolls on its own.
English interface (switchable in the settings), rating history and activity, positions in which you leave opening theory, and a hint in the puzzles tab when the puzzle database is missing.
Opening training: the green arrow now shows on the first move too.
Import your own games as PGN, copy PGN/FEN, clock times and errors in time trouble, update notice, collapsible game list for small screens.
The deep analysis is now offered instead of started automatically; the review column scrolls on small screens and the board no longer jumps.
Reviews open within seconds: a quick preview first, refined in the background.
Move sounds on every navigation step and more reliable sound playback.
Play against Stockfish at 8 levels and review the game afterwards; bot games in the game list. Own sound recordings now play in the installed app.
Board colours and piece sets, wooden move sounds, step through and replay puzzles.
Release packages now include a Flatpak bundle.
First release.
